features.name: AI production maturity
features.description: Captures whether the applicant has shipped AI or LLM-backed systems in production and understands the reliability, evaluation, and hardening work they require.

levels.descriptor: No AI evidence.
Only vague, aspirational, or lightly specified AI mention.
Shows concrete experience shipping AI or LLM-backed functionality.
Shows concrete production AI work plus explicit evaluation, guardrails, correctness, or failure-mode management.

features.name: Academic credentials
features.description: Captures the level of formal academic preparation in computer science or a related technical field that the letter presents.

levels.descriptor: No relevant degree or equivalent preparation is mentioned.
Mentions a bachelor's degree or equivalent.
Mentions a master's degree.
Mentions a doctoral degree.

features.name: Agentic systems design
features.description: Captures direct design or implementation ownership of agent-based systems, including their orchestration, guardrails, permissions, and control boundaries.

levels.descriptor: No agent-based tooling experience is shown.
The letter mentions agents or autonomous workflows only in general terms.
The letter describes a recognizable agent architecture, typically pairing Python agents with Go services.
The letter shows deliberate control design for agents, such as permissions, auditability, bounded actions, or explicit end-to-end ownership.

features.name: Algorithmic fluency
features.description: Captures practical command of data structures and algorithms as demonstrated through concrete engineering improvements or redesigns.

levels.descriptor: No algorithmic strength is mentioned.
Algorithmic fluency is claimed, but without a concrete example.
At least one specific redesign or optimization shows applied algorithmic thinking.
Multiple or especially vivid examples show data structures and algorithms materially shaping system design.

features.name: Collaboration and learning posture
features.description: Captures humility, coachability, and readiness to partner closely with security specialists and other internal stakeholders.

levels.descriptor: Does not mention collaboration with security partners.
Implies support for other engineers, but not specifically partnership with security specialists.
Explicitly states readiness to work with security engineers or build for their workflows.
Shows explicit partnership mindset plus concrete evidence of learning from, serving, or collaborating with security specialists.

features.name: Developer enablement mindset
features.description: Captures whether the letter frames security engineering as helping developers succeed through secure defaults, low-friction tooling, and empathy for internal users.

levels.descriptor: No developer-centered security philosophy is visible.
Shows generic interest in improving security but not specifically in making life easier for developers.
Explicitly talks about secure-by-default workflows, reducing friction, or helping teams do the right thing.
Strongly frames security as developer enablement, emphasizing defaults, tools, or guardrails over policing, process, or documents.

features.name: Engineering rigor
features.description: Captures whether the letter emphasizes correctness, reliability, maintainability, testing, and durable operational ownership in security-sensitive software.

levels.descriptor: Shows little sign of care for maintainability, testing, or long-term operation.
Mentions maintenance or correctness only generically.
Explicitly emphasizes dependable systems, careful engineering, or maintainer habits.
Shows multiple reinforcing signals such as typed or tested tooling, careful releases, production standards, or pride in quiet reliability.

features.name: Evidence specificity
features.description: Captures how concretely the letter supports its claims with specific examples, mechanisms, named systems, or implementation details rather than broad assertions.

levels.descriptor: Relies mostly on broad claims with little supporting detail.
Names some relevant work but gives limited mechanism or outcome detail.
Provides clear examples of work with enough detail to judge fit.
Provides multiple specific examples tied to mechanisms, tradeoffs, or outcomes.

features.name: Go depth
features.description: Captures how central and substantial Go appears in the applicant's real production engineering work.

levels.descriptor: Go is only briefly mentioned or not tied to meaningful ownership.
Go appears in recent work but not as a dominant language.
Go is clearly a main language for backend or service work.
Go is framed as the primary or daily-driver language with substantial system ownership.

features.name: Impact articulation
features.description: Captures whether the letter states the outcomes and observable effects of the applicant's work rather than only listing activities or responsibilities.

levels.descriptor: Lists tasks with no visible outcomes.
Hints at benefit but remains mostly activity-based.
States clear outcomes such as reduced manual work, faster systems, or fewer bugs.
Shows strong leverage language, tying work to capacity, attention saved, or meaningful organizational effect.

features.name: Language breadth
features.description: Captures the range of programming languages the letter presents beyond the core required stack.

levels.descriptor: Shows narrow breadth beyond the main language or two.
Shows moderate breadth across several additional languages.
Shows very broad breadth across many additional languages.

features.name: Narrative quality
features.description: Captures whether the letter presents the applicant through a coherent, memorable narrative or voice rather than as a generic checklist of qualifications.

levels.descriptor: The letter reads like an interchangeable template or a flat list of qualifications.
The letter is competent but generic, with limited individuality in framing or voice.
The letter has a distinctive opening, viewpoint, or sustained framing device.
The letter is memorable and cohesive, with a clear throughline linking the opening idea, past work, and motivation for this role.

features.name: Offensive practice
features.description: Captures ongoing attacker-oriented practice outside routine development work, especially through capture-the-flag or similar adversarial exercises.

levels.descriptor: No offensive-security practice is mentioned.
Shows occasional or casual participation in CTFs or similar practice.
Shows sustained participation in CTFs or other regular adversarial practice.
Shows sustained adversarial practice with strong competitive results or clearly serious investment.

features.name: Open-source stewardship
features.description: Captures responsibility for software used beyond the applicant's immediate team, including upstream fixes, public contributions, and project maintenance.

levels.descriptor: No open-source contribution or maintenance described.
Mentions occasional upstream patches or light contribution.
Shows active contribution or maintenance with review or release responsibility.
Maintains a used project or framework with sustained community, release, review, or user-support responsibilities.

features.name: Ownership seniority
features.description: Captures how much independent responsibility, initiative, and end-to-end ownership the letter claims for the work it describes.

levels.descriptor: Mostly aspirational language or support-role contribution.
Shows some hands-on contribution but limited ownership.
Shows clear ownership of tools, systems, or reviews.
Shows repeated architecture, design, or lead responsibility with independent judgment.

features.name: Personal project ambition
features.description: Captures the technical ambition, complexity, and seriousness of self-directed projects used as evidence beyond the applicant's day job.

levels.descriptor: No side project is mentioned.
Mentions a small or utilitarian personal app or tool with limited technical challenge.
Shows a sustained side project with nontrivial systems, infrastructure, or engineering discipline.
Shows an ambitious distributed, reliability-heavy, or failure-oriented project chosen specifically to tackle hard edge cases.

features.name: Platform leverage orientation
features.description: Captures motivation for foundational infrastructure or platform work whose benefits compound across many teams, products, or users.

levels.descriptor: Does not mention foundational leverage or broader organizational impact.
Expresses a general desire for scale or impact but without a clear platform orientation.
Explicitly wants infrastructure or foundational work that benefits many teams.
Repeatedly frames motivation around downstream leverage, central-platform responsibility, or quiet improvements inherited across an organization.

features.name: Production software experience
features.description: Captures the depth and breadth of the applicant's hands-on professional experience building, shipping, maintaining, and operating real production software systems.

levels.descriptor: Meets the baseline only, with limited scope or a small number of launched systems described.
Shows a solid early-career record, with several years and some repeated launch or maintenance work.
Shows a strong mid-career record, with multiple launches and clear production breadth.
Presents an extensive record for this role, combining years, repeated launches, and broad responsibility across production systems.

features.name: Python depth
features.description: Captures how convincingly the letter shows Python as a serious production language for services, tooling, automation, or agents.

levels.descriptor: No Python experience is mentioned.
Mentions Python briefly or only as light scripting.
Describes regular Python use for tooling, automation, or services.
Shows deep Python ownership across production services or critical internal tooling.

features.name: Role-specific fit
features.description: Captures how specifically the letter explains why this exact role is compelling and maps the applicant's background to the posting's stated responsibilities and requirements.

levels.descriptor: The fit is vague and the reader must infer most of the relevance.
Some relevant matches are stated, but the mapping to the posting is incomplete or indirect.
Clearly connects several experiences to the role's stated needs.
Makes the match easy to verify, systematically covering most of the key qualifications or responsibilities.

features.name: Security assessment practice
features.description: Captures direct hands-on experience assessing systems for security weaknesses through reviews, threat modeling, analysis, and remediation follow-through.

levels.descriptor: No assessment experience is shown.
Shows only general security interest or vocabulary without direct assessment work.
Shows direct experience performing security reviews or assessments.
Shows direct assessment experience plus method detail, such as threat models, attacker mindset, attack-surface mapping, or remediation verification.

features.name: Security automation framing
features.description: Captures how well the letter understands the role's core challenge as scaling scarce security expertise through automation, tooling, and workflow design.

levels.descriptor: Shows little role-specific framing beyond wanting security impact.
Shows general interest in secure defaults or automation, but not a sharp view of the problem.
Clearly frames security tooling as a way to scale review, response, or manual workload.
Frames the problem sharply in terms of scarce expert attention, organization-wide signal handling, variant analysis, or systems-level leverage.

features.name: Security credentials
features.description: Captures the presence and rigor of formal external security certifications or credentials cited as validation of security knowledge or hands-on skill.

levels.descriptor: No relevant security certification is stated.
A baseline or survey credential such as Security+ is stated.
A rigorous hands-on credential such as OSCP or a similarly demanding practical certification is stated.

features.name: Security engineering philosophy
features.description: Captures whether the letter conveys a mature, role-relevant point of view about security engineering as a discipline and the applicant's identification with that mission.

levels.descriptor: Little sign of a security-specific philosophy or perspective.
Expresses seriousness about security, but only in generic terms.
Shows a clear personal lens such as attacker thinking, builder's-eye reviewing, or preference for quiet resilience.
Presents a memorable, role-relevant philosophy that convincingly shapes how the applicant builds and evaluates systems.

features.name: Vulnerability triage automation
features.description: Captures hands-on experience automating vulnerability-report intake, classification, routing, deduplication, prioritization, or related response workflows.

levels.descriptor: No past vulnerability-handling automation is mentioned.
The letter expresses interest in this problem, but gives no concrete example of having automated it.
A concrete example of triage, intake, routing, or report-handling automation is described.
The letter shows strong end-to-end automation of vulnerability handling, with clear workflow transformation or operational value.

features.name: Writing polish
features.description: Captures the mechanical professionalism of the letter's prose, including proofreading, spelling, grammar, and sentence-level polish.

levels.descriptor: Frequent noticeable errors that distract and materially reduce polish.
Several spelling or typographical errors, though the message remains understandable.
Only occasional minor errors; generally polished.
Clean or nearly clean prose with no distracting mechanical mistakes.
